name: Bullpen — Part 5: The market open: where the work waits
description: What runs at the end of Part 5's build. At the market open every request runs now, waits for capacity, or degrades. Orders wait in Postgres (a queued_for_open state the sweeper admits in batches at 9:30 ET), reads and orders use separate bounded pools on one compute, live prices reach every open screen by server-sent events from one read per instance, and three kill switches decide in advance what gives way first. Week one predicted a Market Open Queue and an Order Saga workflow engine; neither was built, because the order is already durable in Postgres before anything else happens.

nodes.name: Bullpen Trading App
nodes.description: The trading app: it owns orders and their lifecycle, reservations, fills, the ledger, positions and the leaderboard view in the trading schema. A stock order placed while the market is closed waits in the queued_for_open state with its reservation; reads (prices, the price stream, the leaderboard, the account poll) and orders use separate bounded connection pools; live prices are pushed by server-sent events from one read per instance; three kill switches turn off handle moderation, the leaderboard refresh and the stream. It also shows end-of-day stock prices read through prices_v1, signs players in with GitHub, moderates handles, and serves the authenticated sweep route the sweeper calls.

nodes.name: CoinGecko

Consent Mode starts denied for all four signals; only analytics_storage is ever granted, and the advertising signals never are (see ADR-0010).

nodes.name: Market Data Service
nodes.description: The single owner of market data: both providers (stocks end of day, crypto) and both call budgets. It serves the public price route and the daily ingest. It is a boundary inside one release, not an independently deployed microservice.

secret-containment.description: The provider keys, the cron secret and the database URL stay in one place: only this service reads them. Everything else in apps/ and packages/ fails check:arch if it names them in code.

config.name: The market-data secrets are read in one place
config.description: ONLY apps/market-data/src READS COINGECKO_DEMO_API_KEY. ONLY apps/market-data/src READS ALPHA_VANTAGE_API_KEY. ONLY apps/market-data/src READS CRON_SECRET.

call-budget.description: A call ledger caps stock calls at 20 a provider-day and crypto at 9,000 a month; a call over the cap is refused before it leaves the process. CoinGecko's monthly volume is also modelled against its allowance.

config.name: Every provider call is counted before it leaves
config.description: A call ledger caps stock calls at 20 a provider-day and crypto at 9,000 a month; a call over the cap is refused before it leaves the process. CoinGecko's monthly volume is also modelled against its allowance.

nodes.name: Bullpen Database
nodes.description: One Neon Postgres project and one database. A schema and a plain database role per transactional owner: market_data (market_data_owner), trading (trading_owner) and handles (handles_owner), with one read-only view each way between owners: market_data.prices_v1 and handles.approved_v1. Orders and the ledger stay in one transaction.

owner-roles.description: ONLY market-data WRITES market_data. ONLY trading WRITES trading.orders AND trading.ledger. ONLY trading WRITES trading. ONLY handles WRITES handles. The runtime roles are plain: no superuser, no bypass, no membership of a role that reads every schema.

config.name: One writer per schema
config.description: ONLY market-data WRITES market_data. ONLY trading WRITES trading.orders AND trading.ledger. ONLY trading WRITES trading. ONLY handles WRITES handles. The runtime roles are plain: no superuser, no bypass, no membership of a role that reads every schema.

migration-folders.description: A migration in one owner's folder that names the other owner's schema fails the build, and fails in the database because each folder runs as its own owner.

config.name: A migration touches only its own schema
config.description: A migration in one owner's folder that names the other owner's schema fails the build, and fails in the database because each folder runs as its own owner.

nodes.name: Alpha Vantage
nodes.description: External market-data API for U.S. stock prices: end of day, one request per symbol, fetched once a day by the Market Data service within a daily call budget (ADR-0008).

status-aware-drift-check.description: A node that names a provider is held to an Accepted ADR: a Proposed one counts as undecided and fails the build (ADR-0016).

config.name: The drift check is status-aware
config.description: A node that names a provider is held to an Accepted ADR: a Proposed one counts as undecided and fails the build (ADR-0016).

nodes.name: Daily ingest cron
nodes.description: Vercel's scheduler: once a day after the U.S. close it calls the Market Data service's ingest, with a secret.

nodes.name: market_data schema
nodes.description: Schema market_data, owned by the role market_data_owner: quotes, the provider call ledger, and the view prices_v1.

nodes.name: trading schema
nodes.description: Accounts, orders with a state and a version (queued_for_open, accepted, working, partially filled, cancel requested, cancelled, filled, rejected), reservations, fills, order events, the ledger, positions and the leaderboard view. Every step of an order's life, including its admission at the open, is one transaction here.

reconciliation-check.description: The materialized view must equal the same ranking computed on read from the source tables; the check names the account and both values when they differ. It runs in CI's database tests.

config.name: The leaderboard view equals its source
config.description: The materialized view must equal the same ranking computed on read from the source tables; the check names the account and both values when they differ. It runs in CI's database tests.

nodes.name: market_data.prices_v1
nodes.description: The price contract: symbol, price, as-of time, source and a stale flag, read-only. The only thing outside market_data that trading may read.

nodes.name: Sweeper
nodes.description: A Vercel Daemon whose only job is to call the Trading App's sweep route and wait: every 5 seconds while an order is open (a queued order counts only while the market is open), backing off to every 60 minutes when none is, and never sleeping past the next 9:30 ET open the route names, so the queued backlog is released on time. It reads no database URL and holds no data. It is built and tested locally, declared in vercel.json, and runs in production deployments only.

secret-containment.description: The sweeper's token stays in one place: only this daemon's source reads it. The route's secret is read only by the trading app's own directory.

config.name: The sweep secrets are read in one place each
config.description: ONLY apps/sweeper/src READS SWEEPER_TOKEN. ONLY apps/web/app/lib/trading READS SWEEP_SECRET.

nodes.name: Neon Auth
nodes.description: Neon's managed sign-in, enabled on the production branch with GitHub as its only provider. The trading app checks the access token it issues against its public keys and stores only the user's id.

nodes.name: Vercel AI Gateway
nodes.description: Vercel's gateway to models, called once per new or changed handle with model typesafe-ai/jev: one Boolean question, is this handle acceptable to show publicly? Only the handle text is sent. A failure of any kind sends the handle to review; there is no fallback model.

gateway-containment.description: ONLY apps/web/app/lib/moderation READS AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY and ai-gateway.vercel.sh. NO trading or market-data code IMPORTS moderation.

config.name: Only moderation reaches the gateway
config.description: ONLY apps/web/app/lib/moderation READS AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY and ai-gateway.vercel.sh. NO trading or market-data code IMPORTS moderation.

nodes.name: handles schema
nodes.description: Schema handles, owned by the role handles_owner: one row per player's handle with its status (pending, approved, review, rejected) and the model's probability, the review queue as a table, and the view approved_v1.

nodes.name: handles.approved_v1
nodes.description: The handle contract: owner user id and handle, for approved handles only, read-only. The only thing outside handles that trading may read, and the reason a pending, review or rejected handle cannot reach a page.
